From natural numbers to real numbers: Rational numbers are p/q; irrational numbers like √2 and π are not. Together they form the real numbers.
Irrational numbers and the number line: Square roots of non-perfect squares are irrational. Between any two numbers there are infinitely many rational numbers.
Decimal expansions: Rational numbers terminate or recur; irrational numbers neither. Recurring decimals convert to fractions by subtraction.
Exponents and surds: Exponent laws and root rules simplify numbers. Rationalising removes roots from denominators.
